slides.0.title: Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage and Saint-Joseph
slides.0.subtitle: The core northern crus
slides.1.title: Hermitage: the famed hill
slides.1.highlights.0.title: AOC and area
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Recognised by the Valence court in 1936 and confirmed as an AOC by the decree of 4 March 1937; in Tain-l'Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage and Larnage (Drôme). About 137 ha in 2025 (69% red, 31% white)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Varieties for red and white
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Red: Syrah at least 85% of the estate's plantings, with up to 15% Marsanne and Roussanne interplanted in Syrah plots; white: Marsanne and Roussanne
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Vin de paille
slides.1.highlights.2.content: A sweet white that may be mentioned on the label: grapes must dry for at least 45 days and exceed 350 g/L sugar at pressing; vintage required; yield 15 hl/ha
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Lieux-dits
slides.1.highlights.3.content: CMS materials list L'Hermite, Le Méal, Les Bessards, Greffieux, Beaume, Péléat, La Croix, Maison Blanche and L'Homme. The specification only requires that a lieu-dit on the label appear on the harvest declaration
slides.1.content: Hermitage is tiny but weighty: yields of 40 hl/ha for red and 45 for white (2024 draft).
slides.2.title: Crozes-Hermitage: the largest northern cru
slides.2.highlights.0.title: AOC and area
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Recognised by decree on 4 March 1937; delimited over 11 communes of the Drôme; still red and white only
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Varieties
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Red: Syrah at least 85% of the estate's plantings, with up to 15% Marsanne and Roussanne; white: Marsanne and Roussanne (no proportions set)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Yield
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Yield 45 hl/ha (ceiling 50); plots with 2.50–2.75 m row spacing capped at 40; minimum natural alcohol 10.5%
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Size (varies by year)
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Inter Rhône 2025: about 2,139 ha (89% red); the INAO text gives 1,700 ha farmed in 2019 — different years and bases, so treat as a sense of scale only, not tested
slides.2.content: Crozes-Hermitage is many times the size of Hermitage, with styles from easy-drinking to structured.
slides.3.title: Saint-Joseph: the long cru on the right bank
slides.3.highlights.0.title: AOC and area
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Recognised by decree on 15 June 1956; delimited over 26 communes (23 in Ardèche, 3 in Loire), stretching nearly 60 km along the right bank; still red and white only
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Varieties
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Red: Syrah at least 90% of the estate's plantings (Drive notes: up to 10% Roussanne/Marsanne); white: Marsanne and Roussanne in any proportion
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Expansion and refocus
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The area was greatly expanded in 1969 (about 6,800 ha plantable); from 1994 it was redrawn and halved to about 3,400 ha, refocusing on the core slopes
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Size and white wine
slides.3.highlights.3.content: About 1,415–1,504 ha (Drive notes and Inter Rhône 2024/2025 — different years); about 86% red and 14% white (white was only 9% in 2005); average yield about 38 hl/ha in 2022; specification yield 40 (ceiling 46)
slides.3.content: 2026 marks the 70th anniversary of Saint-Joseph, a story of expansion, refocus and the re-conquest of the slopes.
slides.4.title: Comparing the three — and common mix-ups
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Position
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Hermitage and Crozes-Hermitage are in the Drôme on the left bank around Tain-l'Hermitage; Saint-Joseph is on the right bank (Ardèche and Loire), like Cornas
slides.4.highlights.1.title: The Syrah floor ladder
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Syrah floors in estate plantings: Crozes-Hermitage and Hermitage 85%, Saint-Joseph 90%; Cornas (100% Syrah) and Côte-Rôtie (80%) are in neighbouring lessons
slides.4.highlights.2.title: White wines
slides.4.highlights.2.content: All three make whites from Marsanne and Roussanne; white share of volume in 2025: Hermitage about 31%, Crozes-Hermitage about 11%, Saint-Joseph about 14%
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Using the area figures
slides.4.highlights.3.content: Areas differ by source year and basis; for exams rely on the relative order — Hermitage smallest, Crozes-Hermitage largest
slides.4.content: Small, medium, large: Hermitage (about 137 ha), Saint-Joseph (about 1,400–1,500 ha), Crozes-Hermitage (about 2,100 ha).
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
For Hermitage vin de paille, how many days must the grapes dry at minimum?
At least 45 days, with more than 350 g/L sugar at pressing.
Which of these northern Rhône crus is the largest?
Crozes-Hermitage is the largest northern cru; Hermitage and Cornas are small and Château-Grillet only about 4 ha.
On which bank of the Rhône is Saint-Joseph, and in which main département?
Saint-Joseph is on the right bank, with 23 of its 26 communes in the Ardèche and 3 in the Loire.
In which year was the Saint-Joseph AOC recognised?
Decree of 15 June 1956; 2026 is its 70th anniversary.
